subject: Memory model phase 2: what each borrowed-parameter rule rejects in std, Ink and Gdev

compilers.wip: wip/memory-phase2-own 0afccb55 on top of 6ad5fbb, same build
compilers.variants: wip plus 2026-11-15-memory-phase2-borrow-rules.patch with `experiment` set to 1, 2 or 3

commands.ink_tests: (in ../ink) blotc migrate-stores <the 62 files of pen.json's tests.files outside tests/rejected> --project pen.json --dry-run --include-std

counting: Distinct (file, span, code) diagnostics from the lowering stage. Every one is borrowed_escape, except one aliased_update in ink/tests/next-improvements.blot:177 that the wip and all variants add.

variants.wip: The branch as written: every parameter, capture and constant that can hold storage is borrowed; a type variable can hold storage; a call whose result type is a function or a type variable is borrowed when an argument is.
variants.1: A store (`=`) or push of a borrowed value is not an escape. A function value is never borrowed, a closure is not borrowed for what it captures, and a call result of function or variable type is not borrowed.
variants.2: Variant 1, and a type variable holds no array inside a generic body.
variants.3: Variant 2, and a return is an escape only when the returned type owns an array: Array, GrowArray, ResizeArray, a list, an opaque type, or data that holds one. Views, references, links and functions only borrow.

notes: Variants 1 to 3 only measure. They add no `own` syntax, no check at call sites and no check that a returned value is unique in itself, so they are not a sound rule set as built.
The measured numbers are the first layer: marking a parameter `own` moves the obligation to its callers.
